# Reference: NLP pocket tools (portable selection summary)

The full matrix, including evidence status, is in `references/NLP_TECHNIQUES.md`. The facilitation prompts are in `references/NLP_POCKET_EXERCISES.md`.

**Rule**: diagnose a problem first, then pick 0–4 tools. NLP is optional. Every tool must pass the transparency test: the presenter would be comfortable telling the audience what they are doing.

| Diagnosed problem | Pocket skill | What it produces |
|---|---|---|
| The talk only sees the speaker's view; WHY feels generic; stakeholders are unclear | `4mat-perceptual-positions` | A 4-position table, with second-position statements marked as hypotheses |
| The vision has no credible HOW, or ideas are killed too early | `4mat-disney-strategy` | Dreamer / Realist / Critic matrix plus one T.O.T.E. demo blueprint |
| The talk is stuck at feature level, or a personal story is disconnected from the model | `4mat-logical-levels` | Level alignment table; optional story-to-model blend at the ratio the user chose |
| Scepticism, a defensive Q&A, limiting beliefs | `4mat-sleight-of-mouth` | Objection matrix: legitimate concern vs. reframe, with claim IDs |
| A flat or abstract script; a long talk with no thread | `4mat-nested-loops` | Common-ground opening, at most 2–3 open loops, language and sensory pass |
| Nerves, flat delivery, aimless stage movement | `4mat-state-anchor` | A rehearsal and state routine, plus optional stage-map cues |

**Never** use covert commands, "unconscious installation", learning-style typing, hemisphere claims, or invented personal stories.
